sentences.en: Do you think it's possible to control someone's attention?
Even more than that, what about predicting human behavior?
I think those are interesting ideas. For me, that would be the perfect superpower, actually kind of an evil way of approaching it.
But for myself, in the past, I've spent the last 20 years studying human behavior from a rather unorthodox way: picking pockets.

When we think of misdirection, we think of something as looking off to the side, when actually the things right in front of us are often the hardest to see, the things that you look at every day that you're blinded to.
For example, how many of you still have your cell phones on you right now?
Great. Double-check. Make sure you still have them.
I was doing some shopping before. (Laughter) You've looked at them a few times today, but I'll ask you a question.
Without looking at it directly yet, can you remember the icon in the bottom right corner?
Bring them out, check and see how accurate you were.
How'd you do? Show of hands. Did we get it?
Now that you're done, close them down. Every phone has something in common.
No matter how you organize the icons, you still have a clock on the front.
So, without looking at your phone, what time was it?
You just looked at your clock, right? Interesting idea.
Let's take that a step further with a game of trust.
Close your eyes. I realize I'm asking you to do that while you just heard there's a pickpocket in the room, but close your eyes.
Now, you've been watching me for about 30 seconds.
With your eyes closed, what am I wearing?
Make your best guess. What color is my shirt? What color is my tie?
Now open your eyes. Show of hands, were you right?
Interesting, isn't it? Some of us are a little bit more perceptive than others, it seems.
But I have a different theory about that model of attention.
They have fancy models of attention, Posner's trinity model of attention.
For me, I like to think of it very simple, like a surveillance system.
It's kind of like you have all these fancy sensors, and inside your brain is a little security guard.
sentences.zh: 这有点像你拥有所有这些奇特的传感器，而你的大脑里面有一个小保安。

sentences.en: For me, I like to call him Frank. So Frank is sitting at a desk.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，我喜欢叫他弗兰克。弗兰克坐在办公桌前。

sentences.en: He's got lots of cool information in front of him, high-tech equipment, he's got cameras, he's got a little phone that he can pick up, listen to the ears, all these senses, all these perceptions.
sentences.zh: 他面前有很多很酷的信息，高科技设备，他有相机，他有一部小电话，他可以拿起，听耳朵，所有这些感官，所有这些感知。

sentences.en: But attention is what steers your perceptions, it's what controls your reality.
sentences.zh: 但注意力会引导你的感知，它会控制你的现实。

sentences.en: It's the gateway to the mind. If you don't attend to something, you can't be aware of it.
sentences.zh: 这是通往心灵的大门。如果你不关注某件事，你就无法意识到它。

sentences.en: But ironically, you can attend to something without being aware of it.
sentences.zh: 但讽刺的是，你可以在没有意识到的情况下关注某件事。

sentences.en: For example, the cocktail effect: You're in a party, having conversations with someone, and yet you can recognize your name without realizing you were listening to that.
sentences.zh: 例如，鸡尾酒效应：您在聚会上与某人交谈，但您可以认出您的名字，而没有意识到自己正在听。

sentences.en: Now, for my job, I have to play with techniques to exploit this, to play with your attention as a limited resource.
sentences.zh: 现在，对于我的工作，我必须利用技术来利用这一点，利用你的注意力作为有限的资源。

sentences.en: So if I could control how you spend your attention, if I could maybe steal your attention through a distraction.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我可以控制你如何分配注意力，如果我可以通过分散注意力来窃取你的注意力。

sentences.en: Now, instead of doing it like misdirection and throwing it off to the side, instead, what I choose to focus on is Frank, to be able to play with the Frank inside your head, your security guard, and get you, instead of focusing on your external senses,
sentences.zh: 现在，我不再像误导一样把它扔到一边，而是选择关注弗兰克，能够与你头脑中的弗兰克、你的保安一起玩，并抓住你，而不是专注于你的外部感官，

sentences.en: just to go internal for a second. So if I ask you to access a memory, like, what is that?
sentences.zh: 只是想深入了解一下内部。所以如果我要求你访问一段记忆，比如，那是什么？

sentences.en: What just happened? Do you have a wallet?
sentences.zh: 刚刚发生了什么？你有钱包吗？

sentences.en: Do you have an American Express in your wallet?
sentences.zh: 你的钱包里有美国运通卡吗？

sentences.en: And when I do that, your Frank turns around.
sentences.zh: 当我这样做时，你的弗兰克转过身来。

sentences.en: He accesses the file. He has to rewind the tape.
sentences.zh: 他访问该文件。他必须倒带。

sentences.en: What's interesting is, he can't rewind the tape at the same time that he's trying to process new data.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他无法在尝试处理新数据的同时倒带。

sentences.en: This sounds like a good theory, but I could talk for a long time, tell you lots of things, and a portion of them may be true, but I think it's better if I tried to show that to you here live.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是一个很好的理论，但我可以讲很长时间，告诉你们很多事情，其中​​一部分可能是正确的，但我认为如果我尝试在现场向你们展示这一点会更好。

sentences.en: If I come down, I'm going to do a bit of shopping.
sentences.zh: 如果我下来的话，我会去买点东西。

sentences.en: Just hold still where you are. Hello, how are you? It's lovely to see you.
sentences.zh: 只要保持原地不动即可。你好吗？很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Wonderful job onstage. Lovely watch, it doesn't come off very well.
sentences.zh: 舞台上的表现非常出色。可爱的手表，但佩戴起来不太好。

sentences.en: Do you have a ring as well? Good. Just taking inventory. You're like a buffet.
sentences.zh: 你也有戒指吗？好的。只是清点库存。你就像一个自助餐。

sentences.en: Hard to tell where to start, so many great things.
sentences.zh: 很难说从哪里开始，有很多很棒的事情。

sentences.en: Hi, how are you? Good to see you. Hi, sir, could you stand up, please? Just right where you are.
sentences.zh: 你好你好吗？很高兴见到你。嗨，先生，请站起来好吗？就在你所在的地方。

sentences.en: You're married, you follow directions well.
sentences.zh: 你已经结婚了，你很好地遵循指示。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you, sir. You don't have a lot in your pockets. Anything down here?
sentences.zh: 很高兴认识你，先生。你的口袋里没有很多东西。下面有什么吗？

This is a task for you to focus on. You have your money in your front pocket?
J: Yup. AR: Good. I won't put my hand in your pocket. I'm not ready for that kind of commitment.
Once a guy had a hole in his pocket, and that was rather traumatizing for me.
I wanted his wallet, he gave me his number.
Big miscommunication. (Laughter) Let's do this simply. Squeeze your hand tight.

(Laughter) Joe, we're going to keep doing this till you catch it.

Squeeze firm. You're human, you're not slow.

Put your other hand on top, would you? It's amazingly obvious now, isn't it?
Looks a lot like the watch I was wearing, doesn't it?
(Laughter) (Applause) J: That's pretty good. AR: Oh, thanks.

Hold your hands together. Your other hand on top.
If you're watching this little token, this obviously has become a little target, like a red herring.

It's not back on your shoulder. It falls out of the air, lands right back in the hand.

Is it in this pocket, sir? Don't reach in your pocket. That's a different show.

So we'd love to give you this lovely watch as a gift.
(Laughter) Hopefully it matches his taste.
We have a couple of other things, a little bit of cash.
And we have a few other things, these all belong to you, along with a big round of applause from all your friends.
(Applause) Joe, thank you very much. (Applause) (Applause ends) So, same question I asked you before, but this time you don't have to close your eyes.
What am I wearing? Audience: Oh! (Laughter) (Hesitant applause) (Applause ends) Attention is a powerful thing.
Like I said, it shapes your reality. So, I guess I'd like to pose that question to you.
If you could control somebody's attention, what would you do with it?
Thank you. (Applause)
